$comment: Ifreglen's app registry. Adding an app is an entry here, not a code change.
kind:
external  a website on the open internet
local     spawn a command, wait for its port, then load it
static    load a local index.html straight off disk
browser   The Wilds, the in-shell browser (one entry, id roam)
capabilities: what the preload exposes to that app. Anything not listed
is simply absent from window.roost. Keep these minimal.
store    key/value persistence scoped to this app
fs       read/write inside this app's own data folder (needs `root`)
shell    open external links in the system browser
apps     see/open/stop/restart other registered apps — the launcher only.
Never grant this to an external app.
bus      publish/subscribe between apps, plus the shell's own system
events (app.started/stopped/exited). Publishing `briefs.file`
files a brief for the phone (lib/briefs.js). Stripped from
external apps in code — a remote page must neither drive nor
eavesdrop.
clip     SHELL-SIDE ONLY. Exposes nothing to the page; tells the shell
to offer clip verbs in its right-click menu and to file that
app's downloads into the Trove. Deliberately NOT stripped from
external apps — external sites are where clipping happens.
liveReload: optional. Defaults on for static apps, off for local (the
dev server pushes its own updates). Never applies to external.
persona: which browser session to use. Apps sharing a persona share
cookies, localStorage and logins; different personas are fully isolated.
Paths and cwds may be relative to this desktop folder or absolute, and may
carry ${ROOST}/${SHELL}/${HOME} placeholders (lib/roots.js). Ifreglen's own
apps live IN this repo under ${SHELL}/apps; Kenoma and Haruspex are outside
projects beside ${ROOST}.

apps.name: Ifreglen
apps.note: Home screen. The 'apps' capability powers its launch tiles.

apps.name: The Wilds
apps.note: The open web, inside the shell. Tabs are ordinary WebContentsViews built as kind 'external', so a page here gets the same stripped capabilities as any remote site and the same right-click clip verbs. Each tab names the persona whose cookie jar it browses in. 'search' is the omnibox template (%s is the query) and "history": false turns off the address bar's memory without touching the Trove. Pins keep the 'curio' jar, which holds a signed-in chat out of the dev (workshop) and work sessions.

apps.name: Lookout
apps.note: Monitoring and research bot (the old Kornbot, rebuilt). Files briefs for the phone through POST /briefs on the bridge, or briefs.file on the bus.

apps.name: Credentials
apps.note: Licences, certifications and renewals. Its data lives under data/apps/credentials (the fs root); a renewal coming due is a brief on the bus (briefs.file).

apps.name: Onboarding
apps.note: New-hire checklists and paperwork. Its data lives under data/apps/onboarding (the fs root); a starter waiting on a step is a brief on the bus (briefs.file).

apps.name: Drafts
apps.note: Letters and emails from templates, drafted by Kenoma when it is up (falls back to the plain template). Nothing is sent from here; you copy it into your mail.

apps.name: Haruspex
apps.note: Antivirus + network security suite. Python HTTP dashboard on :8795. Publishes haruspex.* events on the bus when threats are found; also runs Egress Guard on :8789 (auto-starts with shield) to proxy and mask all browser traffic through threat-sinkholing + optional upstream SOCKS5 tunnel. Starts with the shell so the Wilds' proxy is there from boot; the shell's ',direct://' failover keeps pages loading if it is not. The shell is its only supervisor here: Haruspex skips its own watchdog when XIXOXIS_SHELL is set (the shell sets both that and IFREGLEN_SHELL), and binds its ports exclusively, so a second copy exits instead of piling up (2026-10-13).

apps.name: The Trove
apps.note: Everything you explicitly clipped, with where it came from. Content-addressed blobs plus an append-only index.jsonl — the archive is evidence, so lines are added and never rewritten. ScopedFs confines 'fs' to data/trove. 'bus' means it needs no poll: clip.added reaches it directly. Its Apps tab (data/trove/apps.json, seeded at boot) carries the Professional Goat install and pair codes.

apps.name: Kenoma
apps.note: Coding agent — plug any LLM API, dictate a task, watch it read/edit/run/verify live. Auri's drawer drives the same backend via lib/forge.js; its approvals reach her cards.
